content:
Measurement in Class 2 brings in standard units, telling the time, the calendar and money — practical, everyday Olympiad content. This guide covers what the Maths Olympiad Class 2 measurement chapter tests, the facts to memorise, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 2 Maths Olympiad Measurement chapter tests

  • Length, mass and capacity with standard units
  • Time and the calendar (clock, days, months)
  • Money — coins, notes and simple totals
  • Comparing and converting simple measures

Key facts your child should know

  • 1 m = 100 cm; 1 kg = 1000 g; 1 L = 1000 mL.
  • 1 week = 7 days; 1 year = 12 months; 1 hour = 60 minutes.
  • On a clock the short hand shows the hour; the long hand on 12 means o’clock.
  • 1 rupee = 100 paise; make amounts by combining ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up units (using cm where m is needed).
  • Reading the long hand as the hour instead of the short hand.
  • Slipping in money addition or when giving change.

quiz.title: IMO Class 2 Measurement Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Imran's measuring tape is 1 m long. Jaya's measuring tape is 100 cm long. Whose measuring tape is longer?
questions.explanation: Change both to centimetres (1 m = 100 cm): 1 m = 100 cm and 100 cm = 100 cm. They are equal, so both are equally long.

questions.q: How many Rs 10 notes are needed to make exactly Rs 90 for a colour box?
questions.explanation: Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. It takes 9 notes of Rs 10 to reach Rs 90.

questions.q: A juice stall uses 11 L of orange juice and 6 L of mango juice in a day. How many litres of juice is that altogether?
questions.explanation: Add the two amounts: 11 L + 6 L = 17 L.

questions.q: Asha's jump rope is 1 m long. Bina's jump rope is 95 cm long. Whose jump rope is longer?
questions.explanation: Change both to centimetres (1 m = 100 cm): 1 m = 100 cm and 95 cm = 95 cm. 100 cm is more, so Asha's jump rope is longer.

questions.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
questions.explanation: A pencil is small, so we measure it in centimetres with a ruler.

questions.q: Kabir buys a cricket ball for Rs 78 and pays with a Rs 100 note. How much change should Kabir get back?
questions.explanation: Change = money paid take away the cost: Rs 100 - Rs 78 = Rs 22.

questions.q: A parcel holds a 350 g book and a 150 g pencil box. Together they weigh. How much is that?
questions.explanation: Add the grams: 350 g + 150 g = 500 g.

questions.q: Zoya has a lace 100 cm long. She cuts off 55 cm to make a frock. How much lace is left?
questions.explanation: Take away the cut piece: 100 cm - 55 cm = 45 cm of lace is left.

questions.q: The long hand of a clock is on 12 and the short hand is on 6. What time does the clock show?
questions.explanation: When the long hand is on 12, we read the short hand. It points to 6, so it is 6 o'clock.

questions.q: A flag rope is 4 m long. What is its length in centimetres?

faq.q: How many centimetres are in a metre?
faq.a: One hundred. So 1 m = 100 cm, and 2 m = 200 cm.

faq.q: How do you read the hour on a clock?
faq.a: Look at the short hand — the number it points to is the hour, and the long hand on 12 means o’clock.
